tiles.text: "I'm not a lawyer, I'm a criminal."

groups.name: Justified universe
groups.explanation: Raylan Givens (protagonist), Boyd Crowder (antagonist), Harlan County (setting), and 'You should've run.' (Raylan's pre-shooting catchphrase) are all from the FX series Justified. Walton Goggins was replaced with Boyd Crowder to avoid having an actor name alongside the character he plays.

groups.name: The polarizing 'other guy' in a famous TV love triangle
groups.explanation: Pacey Witter (Dawson's Creek — the electric rival to Dawson for Joey's heart), Noel Crane (Felicity — Team Noel vs. Ben), Jordan Catalano (My So-Called Life — the brooding object of Angela's obsession, rival to Brian Krakow), and Logan Huntzberger (Gilmore Girls — the rival to Jess and Dean for Rory) are all the charged 'other guy' who split TV fanbases in iconic love triangles.

groups.name: USA Network shows whose lead is a skilled professional cut off from their institution
groups.explanation: Burn Notice (spy burned by the CIA), Covert Affairs (CIA operative navigating institutional betrayal), In Plain Sight (US Marshal operating outside normal channels in witness protection), and White Collar (ex-con consultant working under FBI supervision after being caught) are all USA Network shows centered on a skilled professional whose relationship with their institution is fractured or unconventional.

groups.name: TV lawyers whose defining trait is weaponizing the law for personal or financial gain rather than justice
groups.explanation: 'I'm not a lawyer, I'm a criminal.' (Saul Goodman's self-description in Breaking Bad/Better Call Saul), Alan Shore (Boston Legal — brilliant attorney who routinely bends ethics for clients and personal glory), Patty Hewes (Damages — ruthless litigator who manipulates everyone around her for leverage and victory), and Jimmy McGill (Better Call Saul — the origin story of a man who twists legal practice into self-serving gamesmanship) are all TV lawyers defined by using the law as a weapon rather than a shield.
